lecture_beats.subject: proper time, Minkowski signature, restored units, and spacetime dimensionality
accelerated coordinates, equivalence principle, and tidal obstruction
global flatness, normal coordinates, coefficient counting, and the local connection
metric compatibility, regularity, singularities, and pointwise vanishing of Christoffel symbols
pathwise covariant derivative, geodesics, arbitrary-vector transport, and path dependence
holonomy, topology, cone transport, angular deficit, and cone geodesics
sphere transport, tangent cones, small-loop law, and integrated curvature
flat and embedded tori, curvature sign, angular excess, and saddles
spacetime curvature, geodesic gravity, and intrinsic versus ambient transport

resolved_source_issues.issue: Natural-unit and restored-unit proper-time formulas can be mixed dimensionally.
resolved_source_issues.resolution: The chapter states both conventions explicitly and restores spatial factors of one over c squared.

resolved_source_issues.issue: Pointwise vanishing of first metric derivatives can be misread as global flatness, and matching counts can be misread as a proof.
resolved_source_issues.resolution: The chapter separates global and pointwise statements and identifies explicit normal-coordinate construction as the solvability argument.

resolved_source_issues.issue: The metric-compatibility argument is partially circular and assumes regular geometry.
resolved_source_issues.resolution: Metric compatibility is stated as a Levi--Civita property, and smooth nondegenerate metric assumptions are explicit.

resolved_source_issues.issue: The simple coordinate geodesic equation silently depends on the parameter.
resolved_source_issues.resolution: The chapter requires an affine parameter while noting that arbitrary reparameterization leaves parallel transport itself unchanged.

resolved_source_issues.issue: Closed-loop vector return can mix local curvature, topology, and singular curvature.
resolved_source_issues.resolution: Small contractible loops, noncontractible topology, and cone-apex angular deficit are treated separately.

resolved_source_issues.issue: The board symbol R could be mistaken for a later spacetime curvature scalar.
resolved_source_issues.resolution: The chapter uses Gaussian curvature K and identifies the board notation only in its two-dimensional context.

resolved_source_issues.issue: The flat quotient torus can be confused with the familiar curved doughnut.
resolved_source_issues.resolution: The two metrics and their embedding properties are distinguished, including the cancellation of total Gaussian curvature on the embedded torus.

resolved_source_issues.issue: A fixed ambient direction can be confused with intrinsic parallel transport.
resolved_source_issues.resolution: The chapter gives the tangent-plane projection interpretation and keeps the definition intrinsic.

uncertain_sources.note: The spoken phrase infinite curvature is retained only as the singular sharp-cone limit and normalized through finite integrated angular deficit.
The gravity chain is presented as a forward bridge because the field equation and Riemann tensor are deferred.
